methodology.explosiveDefinition: Rewards credible asymmetric upside from overhead room, effective float, rotation/RVOL, catalyst attraction, squeeze/price-discovery potential and risk-to-upside. Penalizes capped upside, exhaustion, dilution/supply, poor liquidity and pump-like structure. Does not override catalyst quality, confirmation or risk controls.

preCatalystEvidenceModel.purpose: Rank pre-catalyst event setups using empirically supported repricing and downside features without treating any feature as deterministic.
principles: Event magnitude matters separately from probability of a positive outcome: prioritize catalysts capable of changing asset/company value materially.
Increase repricing-potential weight for early/small biotechnology sponsors; larger-cap and diversified sponsors generally show smaller event sensitivity.

Increase catalyst-importance weight for Phase 2/3 and Phase 3, especially placebo-controlled studies and adequately/larger-powered trials; Phase 1/1-2 and small exploratory datasets receive less repricing credit unless unusually transformative.
Score trial design, target accrual/power, endpoint quality, prior-phase consistency, safety, regulatory alignment and contradictory evidence separately from market-structure factors.
Apply an asymmetric downside penalty: negative clinical surprises historically produce larger/more persistent abnormal returns than positive results in several event studies.
Do not equate positive announcement language with positive stock reaction; expectations/pricing and other contemporaneous information can overwhelm headline polarity.

Treat pre-event price/volume drift as a secondary context signal only, not evidence of success. Historical oncology work found differing pre-announcement trends but was retrospective, small and potentially confounded.

Explicitly measure priced-in risk: recent run-up, valuation, prior disclosure of headline results, options/short positioning and financing supply can reduce entry quality even when the catalyst is scientifically promising.

Favor extreme-repricing candidates over routine positive-news candidates when evidence quality is comparable; empirical ML research found extreme reaction classes more distinguishable than middle outcomes.
Track outcome windows separately: immediate/1-hour, close/day-1, and day-3; do not assume a positive initial reaction persists.

literatureSignals.sponsorSensitivity: Early/small biotech > large/diversified pharma for typical event-move magnitude.
literatureSignals.stageDesign: Later-stage (especially Phase 2/3 and 3), placebo-controlled designs and greater target accrual showed larger abnormal-return associations in the large 13,807-trial study.
literatureSignals.downsideAsymmetry: Negative trial outcomes can have larger and more persistent downside than positive outcomes' upside; impose explicit failure-loss penalty.
literatureSignals.positiveNewsCaveat: Positive clinical news does not reliably guarantee positive abnormal returns; market expectations matter.
literatureSignals.preEventDrift: Potentially informative but weak/secondary because published oncology evidence is retrospective and confounded; never use as a standalone success predictor.
literatureSignals.marketCap: Smaller firms are generally more event-sensitive; use market cap/asset concentration in repricing potential.
literatureSignals.extremeEvents: Model should distinguish probability-of-success from magnitude-of-repricing and seek setups strong on both.

preCatalystEvidenceModel.validationPlan: Freeze each candidate's score and rationale before the event. Record event result plus 1-hour, day-1 and day-3 returns, maximum favorable/adverse excursion, volume/RVOL and whether the catalyst was already partly disclosed. Recalibrate weights only after a meaningful sample; avoid fitting rules to individual wins such as KOD.

scanMandate.name: Trade Momentum+ small-company event-repricing mandate
scanMandate.objective: Find small U.S.-listed companies where a hard catalyst has both unusually strong public evidence favoring a positive outcome and the capacity to produce an explosive repricing.
scanMandate.coreEquation: evidence confidence + catalyst importance/novelty + transformative economics relative to issuer + repricing potential + favorable market structure - priced-in expectations - failure downside - dilution/supply risk
mandatoryRules: Every fresh scan starts market-wide from scratch; prior tickers do not receive preferential treatment.
Small market cap is a repricing advantage, not a qualification by itself.
Keep evidence confidence and explosive repricing potential as distinct scores; top pre-catalyst candidates should be strong on both.
Biotech clinical/regulatory events and government/DoD/DOE/NASA awards receive strong discovery attention but no catalyst type automatically passes.

Also search M&A, major customer contracts, strategic technology partnerships, court/IP/regulatory rulings, asset sales/strategic alternatives, exceptional earnings/guidance setups and transformative product/commercial milestones.
Prefer hard externally validated events over company-authored promotional announcements; downgrade MOUs, vague partnerships and routine launches without concrete economics.
For government contracts normalize award size to market cap, enterprise value and revenue; distinguish selection/appropriation from definitive award and revenue recognition.
For biotech score prior efficacy, endpoint consistency, durability, safety, powering, trial design, regulatory alignment and contradictory evidence.
Measure how much favorable outcome is already priced in through pre-event run, valuation and prior disclosure.
Evaluate float, liquidity, RVOL/rotation, short interest where useful, balance sheet, ATM/shelf/warrants/convertibles and downside on failure.
Freeze serious candidate scores/rationales before the event and log 1-hour, day-1, day-3, MFE/MAE and catalyst outcome for evidence-driven recalibration.
Do not overfit to KOD; use it as one reference observation while accumulating a larger sample.
priorityDiscovery: Strategic technology partnerships with concrete economics
scanMandate.learningRule: Change weights only when accumulated outcomes support the change; preserve failed and rejected candidates to reduce hindsight bias.
